clue.text: One loose end in simple collection of titles

indicators.note: the first pieces sit inside the word for simple, which is opened up to take them

parts.note: simple means bare, plain and unadorned
taken as written
a tag is a loose end, such as a dangling end of thread or ribbon

explanation.surface: Someone tidying up spots a single loose thread in an otherwise plain collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The baronetage is the whole body of baronets, a collected class of hereditary titles, and also the reference book listing them.

clue.text: Food is short, but never finished

indicators.note: a word that is never finished loses its final letter here

parts.note: short means brief

explanation.surface: A complaint that a meal is skimpy and also never gets eaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese, an example of a food.

clue.text: Jane Eyre accepted her corset after fitting

indicators.note: a corset after fitting has been reshaped, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Charlotte Brontë's heroine agreed to the corset once it had been fitted to her.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase meaning 'the man Jane Eyre accepted': in Brontë's novel she accepts Mr Rochester's proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Charlotte Brontë's novel the governess finally marries her employer, the man whose proposal she accepts.

clue.text: Opera North against search for cross-Channel triumph

parts.note: Norma is an opera by Bellini
con means against, as in pros and cons
a quest is a search

explanation.surface: A northern opera company opposing a hunt for some victory across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera North is a real English company, which hides the split into an opera name and a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Normandy's invasion of England in 1066 was a victory won by crossing the Channel.

clue.text: Dish the league champions?

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef served as a joint, a dish for the table
read as two words, the team at the top of the table is the ...

explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint of beef from the hindquarter, and humorously the leading team is the top side.

clue.text: Very polite senior officer, to whom court rose

parts.note: Gen is the abbreviation for general, a senior officer

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for court is read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a leet was a manorial court in old English law

explanation.surface: A very courteous general, for whom the whole court stood up.
explanation.walkthrough: LEET, a historical manorial court, is an old word the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means refined and well-mannered, overly polite in a genteel way.

clue.text: Strange to keep a rejected part of wall

indicators.note: what is rejected is turned back, so the whole built word is read backwards
the word for strange keeps the letter inside it

parts.note: strange means odd

explanation.surface: Someone finds it odd to keep a discarded section of masonry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts A inside ODD to make ODAD, and 'rejected' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower part of an interior wall, often panelled or finished differently from above.

clue.text: I hear a feature of spring mornings cheers

indicators.note: what the setter hears marks words that are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a dew, the moisture on grass on a spring morning

explanation.surface: Someone notes that spring mornings come with a cheerful greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is a casual British way of saying goodbye, and adieu is a farewell too.

clue.text: Ruined, with justice divided?

definitions.meaning: a marriage or business that is wrecked is said to have run aground ...
split justice into just ice: a drink with just ice is served this way

explanation.definitionFit: Ruined means wrecked, like a ship broken on rocks; a drink served over ice alone is served this way too.

clue.text: Harebell meadow ploughed up for food

indicators.note: a ploughed field is churned over, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A meadow of harebells has been ploughed to grow crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made from wholemeal flour is a staple food.

clue.text: Assume, in short, there's no time to finish

indicators.note: the word loses the T for time from its finishing end

parts.note: short, as in brusque, means curt

explanation.surface: In brief: assume there isn't time to get it done.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a debt or cost is to take it on, which is to assume it.

clue.text: Nature god the first, for me

definitions.text: Nature god the first, for me

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of nature and the wild
taken as written
first is written 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A believer declares that nature's god comes first for them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the belief itself: for such a person nature is god first and foremost.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheist identifies God with nature, so nature as god comes first for such a believer.

clue.text: Member of family meets Santa, say, who introduces one

parts.note: a relative is a member of one's family

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: Santa Claus, Father Christmas

explanation.surface: A family member bumps into Father Christmas at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' is a relative pronoun, the word that begins this kind of grammatical construction.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a relative pronoun such as who begins a subordinate clause describing a noun.

clue.text: Dreadful time to have to cope with parting?

definitions.text: Dreadful time to have to cope with parting?

parts.words: Dreadful time to have to cope with parting?
parts.note: a parting looks like a farewell, but here it is the line combed through one's hair on a day when it will not behave

explanation.definitionFit: A day when the hair is unmanageable has become slang for any day when everything goes wrong.

clue.text: Man with a mission gets dry in a long case

indicators.note: the letters for dry are placed inside the following pieces

parts.note: to long is to ache, as in aching for home
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry

explanation.surface: A diplomat ends up holding a drink-free long briefcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' rounds off the surface, hinting at the attaché case; it is not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a specialist officer on the staff of an embassy, a diplomatic mission abroad.

clue.text: Probing ear, doctor has answer to old complaint

indicators.note: the doctor's letters probe into the word for ear, going inside it

parts.note: lug is informal British slang for an ear
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor examining an ear has a cure for a long-standing ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower back, an ailment, which is one sense of complaint.

clue.text: Judith tucked into this not altogether acceptable set of books

definitions.text: Judith tucked into this not altogether acceptable set of books

parts.words: Judith tucked into this not altogether acceptable set of books
parts.note: Judith sounds like a woman eating, but it is a book of scripture placed in a group not fully accepted as canonical

explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Judith belongs to the writings left out of the Hebrew Bible and many Protestant canons.

clue.text: Woman's on the line — a lot of long-legged chicks here

definitions.text: a lot of long-legged chicks here

parts.note: a woman's means her, the possessive
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the line

explanation.surface: A woman on the phone line describes a crowd of leggy young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicks' suggests young women; here they are young birds in a breeding colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A heronry is a breeding colony of herons, tall long-legged birds, where many young are reared.

clue.text: Language course homework needs picking up first

indicators.note: first places the turned word ahead of the other piece
in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on one's own home
a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A language course where the homework must be collected first.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is a language of Ashkenazi Jews, based on German with Hebrew elements.

clue.text: Ship's valve one vainly displaying newly opened

indicators.note: given a new opening, the word's first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a peacock is a bird that displays its tail, and a vain show-off

explanation.surface: Something on a ship that someone vain shows off once it is unwrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly opened' gives the peacock a new first letter: its P becomes S.
explanation.definitionFit: A seacock is a valve in a ship's hull that lets in or shuts out seawater.

clue.text: Run away from duty, son? Not wizard

parts.note: in the Harry Potter books a Muggle is a person without magical powers

explanation.surface: A son skips his responsibilities, and he is no wizard either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is the smuggler's sense, bringing goods in, and 'duty' is customs duty, not obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: To smuggle is to run contraband goods, moving them so as to avoid customs duty.

clue.text: How cost of beer or sandwiches may be shown, roughly?

definitions.text: How cost of beer or sandwiches may be shown
definitions.meaning: beer is bought by the round and sandwiches are made from rounds of bread, so the bill comes in these units

explanation.definitionFit: Approximately stated figures are rounded off, and a pub bill counted in rounds is quoted in such numbers.

clue.text: Horse circling wide tree

indicators.note: the horse word goes round the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A horse runs round a broad tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree with red berries.

clue.text: Fell-sounding alter ego

indicators.note: a word that is sounding like another is the same when spoken

parts.note: a fell is an animal's hide or skin

explanation.surface: A second self that sounds like the moorland hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' suggests a hill in northern England; here it is the old word for an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Hyde is the evil second self of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's story.

clue.text: Eats a bit of chicken, seeing worsening of economy

parts.note: downs, as in downs a drink or a meal, means eats quickly
a wing is a portion of a chicken

explanation.surface: Someone eats a chicken piece, noticing the economy is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A downswing is a downward trend, as when an economy enters a decline.

clue.text: Cleared out of this Arabic quarter

definitions.meaning: the Rub' al Khali, the vast desert of Arabia, is known by this name as a quarter

explanation.definitionFit: Cleared out means emptied, and the Arabian desert Rub' al Khali is called the Empty Quarter.

clue.text: Ox secured round end of wagon to pull

indicators.note: the ox word is secured round the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a yak is a long-haired Tibetan ox

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An ox is tied round the back of a wagon to haul it.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to give a sudden hard pull.

clue.text: Viciously bear hatred? That's shabby

indicators.note: the letters are attacked viciously and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Fierce loathing of bears is described as a shabby attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare means worn thin to the threads, hence shabby.
